title: In 781, a Maya scholar at Xultun signed a calendar formula linking Venus and Mars, and archaeologists say he may be the earliest named astronomer in the ancient Americas
description: Archaeologists have identified Sak Tahn Waax, a Maya scholar from AD 781, whose name is intricately tied to a mathematical formula inscribed on a wall in Guatemala. This remarkable finding not only illustrates precise tracking of planetary movements and Maya calendar cycles but also highlights individual achievement in scientific endeavors during ancient times. Consequently, Sak Tahn Waax takes the title of the earliest named mathematician-astronomer in the Americas.

title: Mount Olympus, home of ancient Greek gods, is a candidate for the World Heritage List
description: Mount Olympus, the mythological home of ancient Greece’s 12 Olympian gods, may soon join UNESCO’s World Heritage List

title: Baby tyrannosaurs were cat-sized, full of teeth, and more common than scientists expected: A rare fossil clue to how T. rex began life
description: Exciting new fossil evidence indicates that T. rex hatchlings functioned as tiny, cat-sized predators. Weighing just a few pounds and sporting sharp teeth, these juvenile dinosaurs were difficult to unearth due to their diminutive size. Studies show that adult T. rex likely laid around twenty eggs in a single clutch, shedding light on the reproductive habits and early development of these iconic creatures.

title: A major Tasmanian timber processor has stopped taking old-growth logs, backing a shared push to protect the island’s ancient forests as cultural and ecological assets
description: Neville Smith Group will no longer accept old-growth timber deliveries immediately. This decision supports a broader industry effort to protect ancient forests. The move aligns with a "Shared Vision Statement" for sustainable forestry practices. This statement seeks common ground after decades of environmental disagreements. The company's shift is expected to have a limited operational impact.
